changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: For accounts evaluating us or a competitor on acceptance, lead with their own numbers instead of the average: offer a market-by-market view of their own "approvals", with the reasons behind declines, in a form the payments lead can take to the CFO. Suggested line: "Not an average. Yours." See your approvals by market and card type, why each decline happened, and the money left on the table in each market. Say "approvals" rather than "authorization" with these buyers.
changes.why: The average-uplift deck was pitched and rejected with "that's an average. What's mine?" and "I can't take an average to my CFO"; the buyer said "approvals", and the only thing that landed was the market-by-market analysis of his own approval rates.

changes.current_line: Support plans with tiered response times, up to 24/7 coverage.
changes.change: For accounts with a dedicated payments owner: name the person at Stripe who reviews their approval performance every month and brings them findings they can act on, rather than leading with response-time tiers. Suggested line: "A named person at Stripe looks at your numbers every month."
changes.why: The buyer asked who at Stripe looks at his numbers every month and the rep had no name, while the proactive analysis was called the most useful thing we sent him, so he valued an owner of his numbers, not ticket response times.

changes.change: For international accounts that raise "local acquiring" or "local cards, local rails": add a direct, market-by-market answer to that question, paired with an offer to test or diagnose the customer's own traffic by country before a competitor does. Product must confirm what we can offer in each market before this line is used; do not answer with Adaptive Acceptance's machine learning in its place.
changes.why: Adyen won by testing a slice of the customer's own international traffic with results by country, and the buyer adopted "local acquiring" and "local cards, local rails" as his model of the fix, which none of our lines answer.

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: When a new payments leader takes over an account, open with their own declines by country instead of the generic global line. Suggested opener: "Here are your approvals and declines by country, and what we think we can fix."
changes.why: The trigger was a new head of payments whose first move was to pull declines by country, and we did not know he had been hired, so the per-country view he built himself should be our opener.
